article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Nepali OG × Snow Lotus
Breeder: Bodhi Seeds
THC Content: 20%
CBD Content: Generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , Caryophyllene , Limonene
Primary Flavors: Red berry, black cherry, strawberry
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9 weeks / 63 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: High under favorable conditions
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Goji OG arrived during a period when OG Kush breeding was becoming increasingly repetitive, yet Bodhi Seeds managed to take the familiar lemon-fuel foundation in an entirely different direction. Instead of simply making another heavier or more pungent OG, Bodhi paired Nepali OG with Snow Lotus and uncovered expressions that could smell like red berries, black cherry, tropical punch, alpine strawberries, licorice, pine, and gasoline at the same time.

The plant carries unmistakable OG traits, but the fruit underneath gives the aroma an exotic quality rarely encountered in older Kush marijuana. Its effects are equally distinctive: mentally buoyant and sociable at the beginning, more physically settled later, yet generally avoiding the blunt sedation of heavier indica hybrids. For cannabis enthusiasts who value unusual terpene combinations and breeding history, this cultivar remains one of Bodhi’s most recognizable creations.
Genetics and Lineage

Bodhi Seeds created Goji OG by crossing Nepali OG with Snow Lotus. The cultivar is a mostly sativa Bodhi release with an approximately 63-day flowering period, while archived breeder material describes the hybrid as a major OG project that performed successfully both indoors and outdoors. Bodhi named it after the bright red Himalayan goji berry because selected plants produced a distinctive red-fruit character underneath their OG aroma.

The two parents bring considerable genetic depth. Nepali OG combines an OG Kush-type foundation with Nepalese influence, supplying the elongated growth, Kush fuel, resin, and cerebral intensity recognizable in many phenotypes. Snow Lotus—one of Bodhi’s most widely used breeding males—brings Afgooey and Blockhead ancestry into the family. That side contributes vigor, flower production, resin, and an ability to introduce sweeter fruit and floral characteristics without completely burying the OG profile.

Phenotype variation is part of the strain’s identity rather than a flaw. Some plants grow tall and lanky with strong OG stretch, while others develop sturdier branching and heavier flower sets. Aromatically, individuals can range from lemon-cleaner Kush to berry-dominant expressions filled with cherry and strawberry. That diversity made the original regular-seed release particularly attractive to phenotype hunters.
Effects and Experience

The opening tends to feel bright, mobile, and unusually conversational. Mental heaviness is uncommon at first; instead, awareness seems to widen as mood rises and ordinary activities become more interesting. Music can gain texture, conversation flows easily, and creative projects may feel more inviting. Consumer data highlights talkative, relaxed, and tingly effects, reflecting a cultivar capable of maintaining social energy without becoming excessively frantic.

Unlike a pure high-energy sativa , however, the experience does not remain exclusively cerebral. As time passes, a warmer physical sensation begins filling in behind the initial uplift. Muscles loosen without immediately becoming heavy, and the energetic edge rounds into a comfortable hybrid state. Moderate servings can work well for outdoor recreation, creative hobbies, social gatherings, music, or an afternoon when complete inactivity is not the goal.

Higher doses reveal considerably more strength. Concentration can become less organized, time may feel stretched, and the relaxed side of the strain becomes increasingly noticeable. Strong examples are not ideal introductory weed for THC-sensitive consumers. Individual selections and cultivations can reach considerably higher levels, making batch-specific laboratory testing more useful than assuming a fixed percentage.
Medical Benefits

Medical marijuana consumers may appreciate the cultivar most when they want mood elevation without immediately sacrificing daytime functionality. The uplifting mental character can temporarily make stress, low motivation, or persistent negative thinking feel less dominant. Reader-reported data most often associates Goji OG with stress, anxiety, and depression, although those reports represent consumer experiences rather than clinical evidence.

The secondary body relaxation may also make muscular tension and everyday discomfort easier to tolerate. Unlike a very heavy Kush, the plant generally preserves enough cerebral activity that smaller servings may remain compatible with daytime or early-evening use. Appetite can increase as the high develops, while larger doses may become substantially more relaxing.

Goji OG itself has not been clinically proven to treat pain, depression , anxiety, or another medical condition. Research on cannabis and cannabinoids broadly suggests some preparations may provide modest short-term benefit for certain chronic pain conditions, while evidence for anxiety remains limited. THC can also increase anxiety in some people, especially at larger doses. Medical consumers should therefore evaluate cannabinoid testing, personal response, medications, and professional guidance rather than assuming a strain name guarantees therapeutic benefit.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Goji OG’s aroma is the feature that made Bodhi’s original release particularly memorable. Archived breeder material describes full OG aroma and flavor underneath red berries, black cherry, Hawaiian punch, licorice, and alpine strawberries. Modern flower descriptions remain remarkably similar. A 2025 review from Leaf Magazines found black cherry, blueberry, acai, pine, earth, spice, licorice, and a splash of diesel gasoline in the profile.

Myrcene, caryophyllene, and limonene are commonly identified among the leading terpenes. Myrcene is the most abundant, followed by caryophyllene and limonene. Myrcene complements the ripe fruit and earthy foundation, caryophyllene adds peppery spice, and limonene reinforces the sharper citrus and cleaner-like qualities inherited from the OG side. Different phenotypes can shift that balance considerably.

On the palate, berries often arrive before the Kush. Sweet cherry, strawberry, and tropical fruit can occupy the beginning of the inhale, followed by licorice, herbs, pine, and citrus. The exhale exposes more gasoline and earth, giving the sweetness a dry, pungent finish. Certain phenotypes go especially hard toward fruit punch, whereas others taste much closer to traditional lemon-fuel OG with only a berry accent.
Growing Information

Goji OG is capable of excellent production, but its structure requires planning. Archived Bodhi material praised its performance indoors and outdoors, and longtime growers frequently describe certain phenotypes as vigorous stretchers with branches that can become difficult to support once flowers gain weight. Indoor gardeners should expect noticeable vertical expansion after flowering begins rather than assuming the plant will behave like a compact indica.

Early topping and low-stress training can convert that stretch into a productive canopy. Trellising is particularly useful because flexible branches may lean considerably as resinous flowers develop. Removing weak interior growth helps direct energy toward better-lit tops and improves airflow through the middle of the plant. Growers searching through seed populations should also expect meaningful variation in structure, aroma, and finishing time.

A nine-week bloom—roughly 63 days—is the traditional benchmark for Bodhi’s release. Outdoor plants can become substantially larger when given ample root space and sunlight, making support even more important as autumn approaches. Because resinous flowers can hold moisture internally, good circulation and a reasonably dry finish to the season are preferable. Harvest should ultimately be determined through trichome maturity, calyx swelling, and overall plant development rather than an exact calendar date.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Goji OG?
Bodhi Seeds bred Goji OG from Nepali OG × Snow Lotus. The combination mixes OG Kush and Nepalese influence with the Afgooey and Blockhead heritage carried by Snow Lotus.
Is Goji OG indica or sativa?
It is generally classified as a sativa-dominant hybrid. The beginning tends to emphasize mood elevation, conversation, and mental activity, while physical relaxation develops later.
What does Goji OG taste like?
Expect red berries, black cherry, strawberry, tropical punch, and licorice layered over pine, earth, citrus, and OG gasoline. Phenotypes can range from strongly fruity to much more Kush-dominant.
How strong is Goji OG?
Potency varies considerably. Consumers should use laboratory results from the specific batch whenever available.
How long does Goji OG take to flower?
Approximately nine weeks is typical. The original Bodhi release is listed at roughly 63 days of flowering, although individual phenotypes can finish somewhat earlier or later.
Final Thoughts on Goji OG

Goji OG stands apart from the enormous number of Kush hybrids because it expands the OG profile rather than merely intensifying it. Nepali OG supplies the recognizable fuel, pine, citrus, stretch, and resin, while Snow Lotus introduces enough fruit, vigor, and structural diversity to produce expressions that smell like cherry, strawberry, tropical punch, and licorice without losing their Kush foundation.

Its legacy also reflects Bodhi Seeds’ broader approach to marijuana breeding : combining established American genetics with unusual complementary lines and leaving enough variation for growers to discover exceptional individuals. The resulting cultivar can be tall, resinous, productive, highly aromatic, and mentally uplifting while still developing meaningful physical relaxation. For phenotype hunters, classic-genetics enthusiasts, and consumers tired of interchangeable dessert weed, Goji OG remains an enduring example of how distinctive an OG hybrid can become when the breeding goal is character rather than conformity.
